tldr: Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash undercut Claude and GPT on price using domestic chips rather than a cheaper hardware footprint, reported Aug 31. Anthropic answered on Sept 2, cutting Claude Fable/Mythos 5.1's cache price 75% while shipping 70% more output tokens.
whats_new: The newest item in this thread isn't a further price move: T. Rowe Price says it is now using Claude across its investment process, from fundamental research to internal tools -- a customer-adoption signal, not a pricing one.
why_it_matters: A regulated-industry customer publicizing broad Claude use is a real integration data point for teams weighing build-vs-buy in compliance-sensitive workflows -- more informative than another price-comparison chart.

status.detail: Anthropic's Sept 2 cache-price cut stands unchallenged; the latest news in this window is customer adoption (T. Rowe Price), not a new price move.

beats.headline: Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash undercuts Claude and GPT on price, not on hardware
Claude Fable/Mythos 5.1 ships a 75% cache price cut and 70% more output tokens

beats.summary: A regulated financial-services customer, not a further pricing move.

open_questions: After the 75% cache-price cut, how does Claude's effective per-token cost compare to GLM-5.3-Flash's domestic-chip pricing?
Is T. Rowe Price's adoption driven by pricing, capability, or compliance advantages -- and are other regulated-industry customers making the same call?
take_for_builders: Re-run Claude vs. GLM-5.3-Flash cost comparisons against the new 75% cache-price cut, and treat T. Rowe Price's broad adoption as a data point on vendor risk in compliance-sensitive workflows, not a pricing signal.
